root_cause_label: Constraint Violation: Directory Item Limit Exceeded Due to Uncounted Subdirectory
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent designed and locked in a directory-management algorithm that never counted subdirectories as items toward the 30-item-per-directory limit, so the root output directory ended up with 30 files plus one subdirectory (31 items total), violating the spec constraint; the agent's own verification in step 22 explicitly checked only file count and declared success without noticing the subdirectory counted against the limit.
t_err_evidence: compress.py written with flawed directory-switching logic using undefined 'prefix' variable
t_commit_evidence: In step 19, the agent rewrote compress.py with a new get_next_dir() helper that checks only files (not subdirectories) against MAX_FILES_PER_DIR when deciding whether to create a new dir. This rewrite retained the same counting flaw and was executed successfully at step 20 producing the violating structure, making reversal impossible without a full rewrite the agent never attempted.
t_surface_evidence: dir_1 shows 0 files; script reported 52 output files but only 30 part files found
trigger_explanation: The task specification states 'maximum 30 files or folders in each directory', meaning subdirectories count toward the limit. The agent read and acknowledged this constraint (step 6 comment says 'Maximum 30 files or folders in each directory') but implemented the counting logic to track only files, silently ignoring that subdirectories are also 'folders' that count. This is a case of reading the spec but dropping the 'or folders' half when translating it to code.
forewarning_evidence: UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'prefix' where it is not associated with a value
